source_identity.canonical_title: La culture woke est une alliée du féminisme radical

translation.canonical_title: Woke culture is an ally of radical feminism
translation.displayed_title: Woke culture is an ally of radical feminism
translation.summary:
Arriving from the United States like so many other movements, [https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woke woke] culture also imposes its law in France. No one is spared. From the English word “awake,” it brings together all the methods used in a form of moral vigilance against every type of discrimination: permanent alertness to injustice against minorities and women in particular. It models an activism that is sometimes radical and tends to purify social spheres in which some minorities have been oppressed for too long. Today, what we mainly see is the hypersensitivity of “woke” communities—antisexist and representing other intersections such as antiracism and environmentalism—ready to draw the indignant and accusatory digital argument. Are we not heading toward a purified and sanitized society?
In a Figaro article published on 26 January 2021, Benjamin Sire explains: “Twitter’s primary function is now public confession. It gives a major sounding-board role to the neo-Puritan aspirations emerging in a Western world that is more and more frustrated and disappointed with itself, seeking a moral regeneration whose return to the public stage is sometimes disconcerting, especially since, for now, there is no Counter-Reformation or Council of Trent to oppose it...”
For some, the phenomenon goes beyond activism and is also likened to an Inquisition 2.0, bordering on cancel culture and leading to another concept: revisionism of cultural and historical works regarded as “no longer consistent with current ideals.”

citations.translated_citation: There are people who think that to change things, it is enough to judge and criticize others constantly. [...] If I post a tweet or a hashtag about what you did wrong, or about the fact that you used the wrong word or verb, then afterward I can relax and be proud of myself because I am super “woke,” because I pointed the finger at you. But that is not really activism. That is not how change is brought about. [...] the world [was] complicated and full of ambiguities.
